This study is part of a broader research project titled “Human Interactions with Artificial Intelligence in Organizations”, which received IRB approval. All data, analysis code, output, and research materials including the full list of items are available at https://osf.io/ynhtu/?view_only=31642f7caac74082940eb1153d4e9e55. All data were analyzed using STATA MP Version 17.0.

After the experiment, participants completed a post-experiment survey to capture their subjective perceptions during the creative process and received their compensations (see online Appendix A for measures used in survey).

deposits.notes: Also the identical data_url and code_url in forms/c366.json. The printed landing URL returned HTTP 200, but only the OSF JavaScript application shell, which does not establish access to the project or its files. The file-list request https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/ynhtu/files/osfstorage/?view_only=31642f7caac74082940eb1153d4e9e55 returned HTTP 401. The component-list request https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/ynhtu/children/?view_only=31642f7caac74082940eb1153d4e9e55 also returned HTTP 401. Both API responses said "Authentication credentials were not provided." The view-only token was verified against PDF pp. 1 and 16 and was included in both requests. Access is coded account_required because the file APIs explicitly require authentication; whether an ordinary account would suffice or project-specific permission is also needed is unconfirmed. Stopped at that barrier, without logging in or requesting access. The paper claims all data, analysis code, output, and materials for its two experiments (S1 and S2), but file existence, coverage, participant identifiers, arm assignments, scores, texts, and license could not be inspected. Empty files here means no listing was obtainable, not zero files. The separately discovered public registration g49yd identifies this project as its source.

Public preregistration titled "How do Generative AI impact creativity in Experts and Novices?", DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/G49YD, found by the DataCite search for "Meiling Huang". The landing page and https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/g49yd/ returned HTTP 200. Registration metadata explicitly identifies registered_from as project ynhtu, the project cited by the paper, and gives date_registered 2024-03-12. https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/g49yd/files/ returned HTTP 200 and listed only the osfstorage provider. https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/g49yd/files/osfstorage/ returned HTTP 200 with data=[] and total=0; https://api.osf.io/v2/registrations/g49yd/children/ returned HTTP 200 with data=[] and total=0. Neither response had a next page. The public registration text is a protocol, with hypotheses, planned methods, measures, and analysis plans; no participant records, observed outcome scores, or participant-created stories/lyrics were available. It describes the micro-story and lyric tasks corresponding to the topics of S1 and S2, but plans three conditions (AI as tool, AI as collaborator, no AI) whereas the saved paper reports two conditions. Thus correspondence to the final study design is not assumed, and planned sample sizes are not treated as realized counts. Materials_only refers to the embedded protocol text, not uploaded material files or Appendices A-F. API metadata also reports has_data=false, has_analytic_code=false, has_materials=false, has_papers=false, and has_supplements=false. The license relationship https://api.osf.io/v2/licenses/563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e965/ returned HTTP 200 with name "No license"; registration metadata names Ning Li as copyright holder for 2024.

notes: Checked on 2026-10-09 with Python urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1; no login, credentials, personal identifier in request headers, access request, or bot-check bypass was used. Read the entire 103217-character markdown conversion in contiguous chunks, including all references, table notes, and final figures through PDF p. 53. Checked every quoted passage against PyMuPDF text from the indicated page. Quotations preserve wording and punctuation, with layout whitespace normalized. The saved manuscript is the full arXiv paper, not the Academy of Management Proceedings abstract. Appendices A-F are cited but absent from the saved 53-page PDF; no additional appendix files could be obtained. No preregistration statement appears in the saved paper; the related public registration was discovered independently. All paper/form data and code links resolve to the same printed OSF view-only URL. Its HTTP 200 HTML shell must not be interpreted as data availability: the actual file and component APIs returned HTTP 401 with the printed token. Restricted is therefore the data-access finding, although a related protocol is publicly readable. The public protocol has zero uploaded files and zero child components. The publisher landing-page attempt via https://doi.org/10.5465/amproc.2025.16077abstract returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." challenge; stopped there, so journal supplementary files could not be checked. The preprint landing page https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.03963 returned HTTP 200, showed version v1, and had no ancillary/supplementary data-file link. The public manuscript itself is not counted as a data deposit. No public participant-level or participant-linked output data were read. Accordingly, unadjusted arm means, per-person SDs and SEs, analyzed arm counts, assignment/attrition counts, models omitting the post-treatment AI-identification ratio, participant-clustered S2 estimates, and text-based diversity measures cannot be confirmed as computable. The similarity comparison pool, within-person dependence, and missing embedding estimates/precision in final.open_items remain unresolved. Planned preregistration conditions and sample sizes cannot substitute for observed assignments or analyzed counts. Confidence is medium because the principal project and publisher supplements were inaccessible; this result does not establish that the promised data are absent or that access was never public. Only forms/data/c366.json was written.
